articles.title: ‘3 Body Problem’ Director Derek Tsang Boards DEA True-Crime Series ‘Group 41’ From Zhang Yimou’s ‘Shadow’ Producer Jonah Greenberg (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: “3 Body Problem” and “Better Days” filmmaker Derek Tsang is attached to direct and executive produce “Group 41,” a true-crime drama series about the first Asian-American squad at the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA).
body: The project, from Jonah Greenberg ’s Salty Pictures, is at the Taiwan Creative Content Fest (TCCF) in Taipei.

Over the next decade, the underfunded unit grows into an elite international task force. Its targets include Johnny Kon, a Hong Kong boss whose billion-dollar triad spans five continents; Johnny “Onionhead” Eng, a brutal Chinatown gangster; and Khun Sa, a warlord in the Golden Triangle with a 20,000-strong narco-army. The show explores immigration, prejudice and what the American Dream costs, with stories from both sides of the law.

Greenberg, a former managing director of CAA’s China office whose producing credits include Zhang Yimou’s “Shadow,” wrote the source book with Marc Iserlis and Aidan Swift, who are also producers and writers on the series. Greenberg says shows about present-day law enforcement can be great, but surveillance technology now gives cops the upper hand.
“Back in the 1980s when you went undercover, you went deep. And all the bad guys carry guns, and the danger to cops and informants is real,” Greenberg says.

articles.title: Davika Hoorne Returning for ‘Inherit’ Sequel, Director Banjong Pisanthanakun Confirms (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: Banjong Pisanthanakun, the Thai director of horror hits “Shutter” and “Pee Mak,” tells Variety his new psychological horror film “Inherit” will get a sequel, with star Davika Hoorne set to return.
body: “Inherit,” a Centrepiece selection at the Toronto Film Festival, where it world premiered in September, is closing the Jakarta World Cinema festival.

Hoorne plays Woranart, a youthful-looking grandmother who moves in with her granddaughter’s wealthy family. The family soon discovers she harbors a centuries-old centipede spirit with sinister designs on the youngest in the household, Oui (Baipor Thitiya Jirapornsilp).

“The character has to be sexy, beautiful, and funny at the same time. I think of her as a fashion icon, too,” Pisanthanakun tells Variety. “The first image that I have was her wearing a bikini and sunbathing beside the pool, which is very modern. She talks like this [era’s] woman, talking to ChatGPT. She’s a very adaptable girl.”
On set, Pisanthanakun advised Hoorne to study Catherine Tramell, Sharon Stone’s character in “Basic Instinct,” and Anthony Hopkins’ Hannibal Lecter in “The Silence of the Lambs.”

articles.title: AI Filmmaking Platform Core Studio Launches at Taiwan Creative Content Fest With 24 Specialized Agents
articles.summary: Taiwanese technology company imCore Corp. launched Core Studio, an AI filmmaking platform that aims to cover the full production process, from script development and storyboarding to image generation, editing and color grading, at the Taiwan Creative Content Fest (TCCF) in Taipei on Saturday.
body: Guests at the launch included Erica Wang, CEO of TCCF organizer the Taiwan Creative Content Agency (TAICCA), along with representatives from the Taipei Film Commission and imCore’s strategic partners, filmmakers and AI industry professionals.

“Our team understands that professional creators need more than just image-generation tools. They need a comprehensive solution that can genuinely integrate into their production workflows,” said Charles Lee, founder and CEO of imCore Corp. and founder of TWR Entertainment. “Core Studio was developed around the needs of frontline film professionals, transforming years of production expertise into an AI-powered platform that provides more comprehensive creative support for filmmakers.”

The platform’s main draw is a set of more than 24 specialized AI agents that act as a virtual production crew, handling story development, asset generation, visual effects, editing and color grading. imCore pitches them as a way to lower the technical hurdles of AI-assisted filmmaking.

articles.title: ‘Triplets of Belleville’ Director Sylvain Chomet Fires Back at AI Accusations Over Dior Film Featuring Robert Pattinson’s Voice: ‘Everything Was Drawn by Hand’ (EXCLUSIVE)
articles.summary: French animation filmmaker Sylvain Chomet, the four-time Oscar nominee behind “The Triplets of Belleville” and “The Illusionist,” is pushing back against accusations that generative AI was used to create his animated short for Dior featuring a voice cast led by Robert Pattinson, Rihanna, Josh…
body: The controversy flared because Dior positioned “Night in Color” as a celebration of traditional craftsmanship to launch its 2026 holiday season, drawing parallels between Chomet’s hand-drawn animation and the meticulous work of the house’s couture ateliers.

But Chomet and Soumache tell Variety that the film was created using traditional 2D animation techniques, with the characters, backgrounds and key poses drawn by artists. While they acknowledge using automated interpolation to generate some of the intermediate frames that make movement fluid, the pair insists that generative AI was never used to create the artwork.

“Some people are claiming Sylvain was contacted two weeks ago and that the entire film was made with generative AI, without a single drawing, but the reality is that this film took seven months to make and it was entirely drawn by artists,” says Soumache, adding that film employed roughly 20 people, including six animators, alongside storyboard artists, designers, background artists, compositors and editors.
“We used an automated interpolation system for a very small part of the process, but the film itself is traditional 2D animation,” says the French producer.

articles.title: Sebastián Lelio was a fascinating film-maker of great passion and poetry
articles.summary: Chilean director of films including Gloria and A Fantastic Woman could expertly capture both the personal and political. Sebastián Lelio, director of A Fantastic Woman and Gloria, dies aged 52. The last 20 years have seen an amazing flowering of creativity from Chilean film-makers.
body: But there can hardly be a director who dramatized the different aspects of Chile’s complex and conflicted 21st-century zeitgeist than Sebastián Lelio. Some of his films were political and some not obviously political. But they were all fierce, passionate and sensual – an expression of defiance, at some level, against a system which robbed ordinary people of pleasure.

Lelio’s 2017 film Disobedience, his English-language debut, starring Rachel Weisz and Rachel McAdams, was a London-set movie about a conservative Jewish community in which Weisz plays Ronit, a rabbi’s daughter whose secret gay identity flowers once her father is dead in circumstances of unbearable tension. It is a fascinating film, all the more intriguing perhaps in that it is happening outside Lelio’s Latin American heartland under gray British skies.
points: Chilean director of films including Gloria and A Fantastic Woman could expertly capture both the personal and political.

articles.title: Relief, tears and sadness: Married at First Sight UK cast react to show being axed
articles.summary: It was cancelled after a BBC Panorama investigation heard allegations from three former cast members.
body: "I'm delighted and so relieved no-one else will have to go through the same again."
That's what one woman - who alleged she was raped on Married at First Sight UK - texted to me, as the news broke that the show was being cancelled.

Another woman, who also says her on-screen husband raped her, was in tears at the news. She told us she felt "great, consuming relief", but added she was "astounded" it had taken an external review for Channel 4 to finally pull the plug on the show.

Commenting on the review, she said: "Suggesting the programme could reasonably continue with the implementation of a 'safe word', 'panic button' or 'lockable bathroom with an extra bolt inside' is absolute insanity to me."

articles.title: 5 Years Ago: Benedict Cumberbatch Starred In Netflix's Best Western Movie
articles.summary: Five years ago, Benedict Cumberbatch led the ensemble cast of Netflix's best Western, one of the very best original films the streamer has ever released.
body: Jane Campion's 2021 film "The Power of the Dog," released five years ago this month, was one of the best films of its year. It was widely praised by critics and by the Academy, despite earning a tiny handful of cash during its not-very-wide theatrical release. The film was nominated for an astonishing 12 Academy Awards, including Best Picture, making it the seventh Netflix film in four years to be nominated in the top category (other nominees included "Roma," "The Irishman," "Marriage Story," "Mank," "The Trial of the Chicago 7," and "Don't Look Up"). "The Power of the Dog" ultimately only won one Oscar, for Best Director.

articles.title: Skepta: 'I'm what it looks like if you give an immigrant child a chance'
articles.summary: The grime artist, widely considered to be one of the UK's best, returns with his first album in seven years.
body: One of the biggest names in grime is back - and he's picked his moment.
"Finally," Skepta promises BBC Newsbeat, "some good rap music, some good UK grime sounds."

The Fork and Knife has been a long time in the making. Seven years on from his last album, Ignorance Is Bliss, and more than two years since it was first teased, the rapper knows how to keep fans waiting.
And with a Mercury Prize, a Brit and two Ivor Novello Awards under his belt, greatness is no less than what fans expect from this titan of the rap scene.

articles.title: Gladiator II stuntman sues over injuries from on-set explosion
articles.summary: Edward Sarsfield says he suffered "excruciating" burns while filming a scene on a burning ship.
body: Edward Sarsfield was playing a dead soldier in the movie in 2023 when a gas line used for special effects exploded on the vessel, causing 20ft flames that made his costume catch fire, his legal claim said.
He "panicked and ran" before colleagues threw bottles of water over his burns, which covered about 15% of his body, including his face, his arms and hands, he said.
Sarsfield is suing August Street Films, whose defence said it admits liability for the accident, but has not made an admission about the alleged injuries or agreed to the requested £200,000 damages.
Gladiator II, released in 2024, was the long-awaited sequel to the hit 2000 drama starring Russell Crowe. The follow-up was directed by Sir Ridley Scott and starred Paul Mescal and Denzel Washington.

articles.title: The Cat in the Hat review – Bill Hader brings plenty but this animated rework is a mess
articles.summary: The SNL alum has an appealing energy and this is an improvement on the 2003 travesty but it’s also far too long and strangely corporate. Over a long enough timeline, perhaps every living alumnus of Saturday Night Live will play the Cat in the Hat.
body: Just to be clear, this is the same studio that passed on releasing not one but two well-liked features starring their trademark Looney Tunes characters in the last few years. (Puzzlingly, a new Looney Tunes short starring Daffy Duck nonetheless debuts in front of this movie.) Warner has one of the most storied animation libraries in American cinema (and, for that matter, plenty of great animated TV shows like Batman: The Animated Series and Animaniacs) but as far as features go, they’ve never settled on a clear creative vision. They seem just as adrift in a landscape crowded with serious competitors as they were back when everyone was imitating Disney.

When the Cat arrives, he eventually – the movie’s set-up, midsection and climax are all painfully distended – whisks the kids and their suddenly talking goldfish Waffles (Matt Berry, the other vocal MVP of the cast) into a series of magical lands expanded from the family’s possessions. They’re in search of the Cat’s Go-Backer device, which Gabby hopes to use to undo their family’s move, and pursued by a shadowy, gigantic creature called Something.

articles.title: If Dune is this generation’s Star Wars, we are all in big trouble
articles.summary: According to Florence Pugh, Denis Villeneuve’s stunningly strange and breathtaking universe is the equivalent to George Lucas’ heroic space opera. Let’s hope not. A long time ago, far far away, in a galaxy called the 1970s, kids dreamed of joining the rebellion, rescuing a princess and blowing up…
body: It is worth remembering this when considering Florence Pugh’s recent declaration, ahead of next month’s Dune: Part Three, that Dune is her generation’s Star Wars. And then wondering how much trouble we might be in if she’s actually right. “I think they brought back movie-going. What an event the second [Dune] was,” Pugh cheerfully told the New York Times. “It was just so lovely to be a part of something that we know is our generational kind of Star Wars.”

Pugh’s analogy becomes stranger the more you think about it. Lucas may have drawn heavily on Frank Herbert’s original 1965 book when he dreamed up the desert planet of Tatooine, but the two sagas offer distinctly different views of the universe. The original Star Wars trilogy asked us to believe that its central villain was ultimately worthy of redemption, despite having been a powerful cog in a regime responsible for billions of deaths. Dune, by contrast, is flowing grimly in exactly the opposite direction.
